summary: Extends the myseliasan Fleet Map (shipped as a single-node-pin geographic view) into a building-oriented digital twin: a Site now carries its own Lat/Lon/MapPlaced and an operator-chosen icon glyph, so a building - not the appliance that happens to record its cameras - is what anchors cameras on the geographic map. GET /api/sites/overview rolls up every building for the map (worst status among the nodes with cameras inside it, plus per-camera unread-notification counts via a new GET /api/notifications/tally, so one node recording cameras in several buildings is never double-counted onto all of them). A node can be dragged onto a building (or picked from a 'needs a home' list) to record that it physically resides there (PUT /api/nodes/{id}/building, ManagedNode.SiteId); a building-resident node stops drawing its own map pin and is represented by its building's marker instead. Clicking a building marker opens a new building-scoped floor-plan drill-down (GET /api/sites/{id}/floorplans, BuildingFloorView) showing every floor with every camera on it regardless of which node owns each one, each marker/coverage-wedge colored and streamed by its own owning node - distinct from the existing node-scoped floor view. The indoor floor-plan editor gained a proper create/edit building dialog (name + curated emoji icon picker, replacing a bare name prompt), pan/zoom + a select/delete toolbar for the plan canvas, keyboard delete/escape for the selected marker, and flags a placement as a 'ghost marker' when its camera no longer exists on an online, reachable node. The camera live window can now open a recorded event's snapshot/clip inline over the same live panel (a Back button returns to live without tearing down the underlying WebRTC stream). The offline basemap moved from a single .pmtiles archive to a directory of region archives (GET /api/basemap/tiles/{name}, region bounds parsed straight out of each PMTiles header) so a fleet spanning disjoint areas is served as several region files instead of one planet-sized archive, and gained an optional, off-by-default on-demand region download (POST /api/basemap/download, gated behind an operator- or env-configured remote pmtiles source plus the pmtiles CLI tool) - the one action in this otherwise air-gapped app that can reach the internet, and only when explicitly configured.
compatibility: Backward compatible and additive. New Site.Lat/Lon/MapPlaced/Icon and ManagedNode.SiteId columns are added by explicit, idempotent, NULL-backfilling migrations in app.go's Migrations() that run before and independently of autoMigrate, so an upgrade never 500s on a missing column. Every existing site defaults to unplaced (0/0/false) and every existing node defaults to SiteId 0 (building-less) - nothing already on the map moves or disappears; an operator opts in to the building model by dragging a building onto the map and/or assigning nodes to it. The basemap directory convention (<dataDir>/basemap/*.pmtiles) replaces the old single <dataDir>/basemap/basemap.pmtiles path but remains backward-compatible: an existing basemap.pmtiles file sitting in that directory is picked up unchanged as one region. Remote region download stays off unless an operator explicitly sets MYSELIASAN_BASEMAP_SOURCE or the runtime PUT /api/basemap/config source - an install that never configures it is exactly as offline as before. This is a myseliasan-scoped feature and does not touch mymatasan, myidsan, or myiotsan.
